title: Check yourself: Submitting a batch: shape, limits and price

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A team has 40,000 classification requests, none needed before tomorrow, on Claude Sonnet 5.5. What does the page support?

options.text: Send them as a batch with `stream: true`, so results arrive as they finish
options.says: Ruled out because "Batch results come back as a single file, not a stream."

options.text: Send them as a batch at the standard price, since a batch only helps throughput
options.says: Ruled out because the discount covers "input, output and special tokens" at half price.

options.text: Send them one by one, since a batch cannot take more than a few hundred
options.says: Ruled out because "A Message Batch is limited to either 100,000 Message requests or 256 MB in size", which is far above a few hundred.

options.text: Send them as a batch, at 50% of the standard price, and read the results later
options.says: The page says "All usage is charged at 50% of the standard API prices" and that the batch suits work where "Immediate responses are not required".

questions.stem: A batch request body copied from a live endpoint contains `speed` set to fast. What is the outcome for that request?

options.text: A validation error comes back, since that parameter is unsupported here
options.says: The page says these parameters are "refused with a validation error".

options.text: The batch runs at the fast rate, since the parameter is passed through unchanged
options.says: Ruled out because "Fast mode tunes synchronous latency, which doesn't apply to asynchronous batch processing."

options.text: The parameter is dropped silently, and the batch runs at the standard rate
options.says: Ruled out because the page says they are "refused with a validation error", not dropped.

options.text: The batch is accepted, but the fast rate is billed in place of the discount
options.says: Ruled out because "All usage is charged at 50% of the standard API prices", with no fast rate in a batch.

questions.stem: A job has 250,000 small requests. How must it be submitted?

options.text: In two batches, since each holds up to 128,000 requests
options.says: Ruled out because the stated limit is "either 100,000 Message requests or 256 MB", not 128,000.

options.text: In one batch, since the size limit is counted in bytes and not in requests
options.says: Ruled out because "whichever is reached first" means the request count limit applies as well as the size.

options.text: In at least three parts, since one batch holds 100,000 items at most
options.says: The page says "A Message Batch is limited to either 100,000 Message requests or 256 MB in size, whichever is reached first", so 250,000 needs three.

options.text: In one batch, and the system splits it into parts by itself
options.says: Ruled out because the splitting is the client's job: "whichever is reached first" is a limit on what you submit, and the practice's `split_batches` does the cutting.
